verdict.rationale: Galileo's official MCP server lets an agent in an IDE create and manage datasets and run experiments. A published OpenAPI spec with 202 /v2 paths suggests programmatic access, but the pack never shows how an agent reads back experiment results or metric scores. missing for 10: documented retrieval of eval/experiment results via MCP/API/SDK, named dataset and experiment endpoints or SDK calls, hands-on corroboration of the end-to-end agent loop.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have an agent create a dataset, trigger an eval run programmatically, and read back the results

citations.quote: With MCP, you can access Galileo's capabilities directly from your development environment, including: Creating and managing datasets, Running experiments

The Galileo Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enables seamless integration between AI-powered IDEs, such as Cursor, or VS Code with GitHub Copilot, and Galileo's evaluation and observability platform.
Galileo publishes a downloadable OpenAPI 3.1.0 document at its API origin (202 paths, all under /v2/)
